Use project slug `issue-3` and write exactly these three files (and nothing else): - `.autose-work/spec/SRS-issue-3-v1.md` - `.autose-work/spec/REG-issue-3-v1.md` - `.autose-work/spec/VAL-issue-3-v1.md` External-evidence (MCP/Fetch) checks are not available here: report them as NOT-RUN. Additional rules for this pipeline (they take precedence over the skill where they differ): 1. Requirements describe observable behaviour of the library, not code design. You may read the code (e.g. to learn the current output format) but do not plan the change. 2. Every functional requirement has acceptance criteria written on ONE line each, exactly as `- AC-FR-001-1: Given , when , then .` Use concrete example inputs and expected HTML fragments so each AC becomes one pytest test. Avoid vague words (fast, simple, robust, large, secure, …). 3. Add acceptance criteria that existing behaviour the issue does not ask to change stays the same (regression), where the change could plausibly break it. 4. At most 6 functional requirements. Keep the documents short. 5. If the issue is vague, choose the most reasonable interpretation, record it as an assumption (ASM-*) and an open question (OQ-*), and still write testable ACs for that interpretation. We render user-generated content (forum posts) with mistune. For SEO-spam reasons we need every link to carry `rel="nofollow ugc"`. Right now we post-process the HTML with a regex, which is fragile. Could the HTML renderer get an option for this? Something like: ```python renderer = mistune.HTMLRenderer(link_rel="nofollow ugc") md = mistune.create_markdown(renderer=renderer, plugins=["url"]) md("[site](https://example.com)") #

site

``` It should apply to every `` the renderer produces (normal links, `` autolinks, plain URLs from the url plugin). Images shouldn't be affected. Default behaviour (no option) should stay exactly as it is today. Happy to test a PR. Thanks for the great library!

INFERRED items are never READY. ## 1. Introduction ### 1.1 Purpose This specification defines requirements for adding a `link_rel` configuration option to `HTMLRenderer` in the mistune Markdown parsing library to support rendering anchor tags with specified `rel` attribute values. ### 1.2 Problem statement (as given) Users rendering user-generated content with mistune currently post-process rendered HTML using regular expressions to add `rel="nofollow ugc"` to links for SEO-spam prevention, which is fragile. The issue requests that `HTMLRenderer` accept an option (such as `link_rel="nofollow ugc"`) applied to every anchor tag produced by the renderer (including normal links, autolinks, and URL plugin links) while leaving images unaffected and preserving default behavior when no option is provided. ### 1.3 Scope - **In scope (stated):** Adding a `link_rel` parameter to `HTMLRenderer` initialization, applying `link_rel` to normal links, autolinks, and URL plugin links, excluding images from `link_rel`, and preserving default behavior when `link_rel` is not provided. (SRC-001, SRC-002, SRC-003) - **In scope (inferred, pending confirmation):** None. - **Out of scope:** See OOS-001 through OOS-003 in the register. ### 1.4 Success measures All functional requirements pass automated pytest tests verifying correct HTML generation with `link_rel` and backward compatibility. ## 2.
